title: Inertia and Frame-Dragging in the Observable Universe
content: In the time of Galileo and Newton, inertia was understood as a property of absolute space. Later, it was interpreted as a consequence of the gravitational influence of distant matter. Einstein suggested that this influence is related to frame-dragging, a phenomenon arising in general relativity. In this work we pursue this idea by using the frame-dragging components corresponding to Coriolis and linear acceleration. By integrating these contributions over the mass of the entire observable universe, one should obtain a value close to the classical Coriolis or linear inertial acceleration. This provides a quantitative test of Einstein's hypothesis.Within the approximations adopted here, the resulting values are indeed consistent with this hypothesis.
